subject: Datacorp private offer on AWS Marketplace — term length, approvals, and activation plan
messages:
From: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@datacorp.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@datacorp.com
Date: 2027-04-28T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer inquiry — term options & approvals

Hi Vivek / Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. We want to move forward with Redwood on AWS Marketplace but need to understand a couple of things before we create the private offer on our side:

- Term length: our procurement team is pushing for a 24-month pricing commitment for better unit economics; finance prefers 12 months with a review after 9 months. Is Redwood able to support both options as separate SKUs or do you prefer a single canonical term?
- Buyer approvals: for deals over $200k our buyer routing requires procurement + legal + CFO signoff. Who at Redwood needs to be looped for activation and acceptance in the Marketplace console?
- Evidence: our security team will need SOC2 scoping details, data residency, and a short list of the onboarding artifacts we should submit with the PO.

We'd also like an estimate of how long activation takes once the private offer is created by us (we have an internal vendor approval window of 10 business days). Can you attach the pricing grid and the SOC2 summary for the reviewers?

Next steps: if you can send a short checklist for buyer approvals and an estimated timeline we can draft the PO this afternoon.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Sharma
Head of Cloud Procurement, Datacorp
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@datacorp.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — term options & approvals

Rajiv — thanks, this is straightforward. Quick answers up front and a proposed activation path.

1) Term modeling and SKUs
- We can support both 12-month and 24-month private-offer SKUs. Practically we often structure as: a 12-month SKU (standard) and a 24-month SKU with a discount tier. If Datacorp prefers a single PO we can accept a 24-month PO and apply the discount on our end (we will return a price attachment).

2) Buyer approvals / activation owners
- Buyer routing you described (procurement + legal + CFO) is fine. From Redwood's side:
  - Contract & Marketplace signoff: Vanessa Ortiz (cc) — she handles Seller Console acceptance and any DocuSign routing for redlines.
  - Finance invoicing/proration: Neha Kapoor (cc) — handles billing cadence and invoice triggers.
  - Security evidence: I will attach the SOC2 summary and a short onboarding artifact list for your security reviewer.

3) Evidence and artifacts (what to attach to PO)
- SOC2 Type II summary (attached: SOC2_summary.pdf)
- Short environment diagram and data flow (we provide template)
- List of redaction/retention controls and KMS integration notes
- IP & support SLA clause to include in the DocuSign (if needed)

4) Timeline & activation steps (proposed)
- Day 0: Datacorp submits private offer in AWS Marketplace and notifies us (include PO number and HubSpot deal id).
- Day 1–2: Redwood validates the PO fields and pricing, confirms co-sell entitlements (if applicable).
- Day 2–4: Acceptance in Seller Private Offers console and DocuSign routing for contract redlines (if any).
- Day 5–10: AWS buyer-side approvals (procurement/legal/CFO). Once buyer signs, the private offer activates immediately on Marketplace.

Given your 10-business-day vendor window, plan on a conservative 7–10 business day cadence from PO submission to activation assuming no redlines. If you need faster activation we can provisionally accept a 12-month pilot (pilot SKU) that can be converted on the Marketplace UI to a longer term after approval.

Attachments: pricing_breakdown_v2.xlsx (pricing scenarios for 12/24 mo) and SOC2_summary.pdf.

Proposed immediate next step: Vanessa, can you confirm the DocuSign template we will use and whether we need a special co-sell opt-in mapping for Datacorp?

— Vivek
VP, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@datacorp.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — term options & approvals

Rajiv / team — adding a few operational details from the Marketplace ops side so your procurement and legal teams have clarity:

- Seller acceptance: Once Datacorp creates the private offer, the offer appears in our Seller Private Offers console. We accept the offer and (if needed) trigger DocuSign for contract language changes.
- Co-sell: If Datacorp wants to enable AWS co-sell we need to confirm entitlement mapping on the listing (product SKUs) and opt-in flags. Co-sell does not change buyer approvals but does affect how consulting credits/marketing credits are recorded.
- Term structure recommendation: To balance risk and onboarding, we often propose a split approach for new enterprise buyers: a 6-month pilot SKU (reduced commit) followed by a 12–18 month renewal SKU that triggers a price discount. This reduces vendor approval friction and gives your security team time for production validation.
- Activation checklist (high level): see attached datacorp_mop_activation_checklist.pdf — includes required fields for the PO, recommended DocuSign clauses, and a list of evidence items for security.

Note on redlines: If legal insists on non-standard Data Processing Addendum language, please flag that up front. Redlines can add 3–5 business days. For a faster activation, we can accept the standard Redwood/Marketplace terms and follow up with a separate Master Services Agreement executed outside of Marketplace.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute align with your procurement + security this week to walk through the checklist.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Marketplace Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — term options & approvals (finance notes)

Internal—quick finance notes to loop into the thread so Rajiv's team has expectations:

- Billing cadence: Redwood can invoice annually upfront (preferred for 24-month) or monthly invoice for usage-anchored SKUs. For PO-based marketplace activation we normally bill monthly by default unless buyer requests upfront invoicing.
- Proration: If Datacorp requests mid-cycle term changes we prorate at the time of conversion; finance needs the HubSpot deal id and the PO number to correlate invoices.
- Revenue recognition: to keep compliance simple for you, mark the PO as a Marketplace private offer with the seller acceptance date as the activation date.

I've added the HubSpot link to the related links; once the PO is submitted please include the HubSpot deal id (or we can create one for tracking).

—Neha
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@datacorp.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — term options & approvals

Thanks all — that helps a lot. Two quick items:

1) Procurement will draft a 24-month PO today and include procurement@datacorp.com + CFO on the approval chain. Expect our PO number in this thread by EOD tomorrow.
2) Security has asked for a short-lived UAT environment access (read-only) to smoke test before activation — is that something Redwood can provide for a 2-week window? If yes, we can attach a UAT request and it will speed up our internal approval.

If you can confirm the UAT approach (contact + timeline), we'll kick off the PO. Appreciate the speedy turnaround.

—Rajiv
